claims.claim: Lockheed Martin sits on several defense-capability bottlenecks where missile/interceptor production, combat-aircraft integration and space command/navigation infrastructure translate government and allied security demand into physical capacity requirements.

The causal path is not backlog-to-value automatically: funding/definitization, specialized supply chains, production ramps and program execution determine whether strategic demand converts into durable cash economics.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Record $230.4B backlog and large Missiles and Fire Control backlog expansion are consistent with constrained defense-production demand, including PAC-3/THAAD and other munitions ramps.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Demand spans air/missile defense, tactical missiles, combat aircraft, undersea systems and strategic/space programs rather than one end market.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Mission integration, installed programs and qualification barriers create friction, but budget reprioritization, competing platforms and alternate suppliers can shift future awards.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Production ramps demonstrate capacity expansion, while specialized components and ramp execution remain explicit constraints.

risks.risk: Successor bottlenecks are specialized supply availability, funded contract structure and production-ramp execution rather than demand alone.
Government/allied concentration makes budget, authorization and export decisions structurally important to conversion timing.

causalEdges.mechanism: government/allied requirements create funded procurement and replenishment demand
causalEdges.falsifier: funded awards and backlog weaken despite persistent stated security need

causalEdges.mechanism: qualified program positions and integration capability convert awards into contracted workload
causalEdges.falsifier: competitors capture awards or cancellations materially erode backlog

causalEdges.mechanism: successful execution converts contracted workload into deliveries, profit and cash
causalEdges.falsifier: contract assets, program losses or working-capital absorption rise persistently despite sales growth

contradictions.claimA: Record backlog and production ramps support long-duration demand visibility.
contradictions.claimB: Cash conversion and program economics have shown material timing and execution volatility.
contradictions.disposition: Both can be true; demand visibility is structural evidence, while realized economics remain execution-dependent and should not be inferred from backlog alone.

unknowns.unknown: Reviewed Beta evidence does not quantify supplier-level concentration for critical missile, aircraft and space components.

claims.claim: Current demand evidence is strong, but 2026 year-over-year profit comparisons benefit materially from the absence of $1.6B of 2025 reach-forward program losses; headline profit growth therefore should not be read as pure underlying operating leverage.
Q2 2026 free cash flow of $2.9B was helped by timing of customer receipts and lower tax payments, so a single quarter does not resolve cash-conversion volatility.
No current Beta evidence establishes a material dilution or governance defect; those risks remain unasserted rather than manufactured.

factors.name: thesisQuality
factors.basis: Strategic demand and backlog are well supported, but economics remain exposed to program accounting, contract structure and execution.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: Sales grew 11% and guidance rose, while profit comparability is flattered by prior-year reach-forward losses and cash flow benefited from receipt timing.

factors.name: pricingPower
factors.basis: High demand does not imply unrestricted pricing because government procurement and contract structures constrain economics.

risks.risk: Backlog can overstate near-term economic realization when funding, definitization, delivery schedules or working capital delay conversion.
Fixed-price and complex development programs can generate reach-forward losses even in a strong demand environment; 2025 included $1.6B of such program losses.
Customer concentration in governments and allies creates budget, political, export and procurement exposure.
Specialized supply-chain and ramp constraints can prevent strategic demand from becoming deliveries on expected timing.

causalEdges.mechanism: cost growth or schedule changes can require unfavorable profit adjustments or reach-forward losses
causalEdges.falsifier: sustained absence of material unfavorable adjustments across major programs while ramps scale

contradictions.claimA: Q2 2026 operating profit increased sharply year over year.
contradictions.claimB: A large portion of the comparison reflects $1.6B of prior-year reach-forward losses rather than solely current-period productivity.
contradictions.disposition: Resolved as a comparability issue, not a blocker; retain underlying sales/ramp evidence separately from year-over-year profit optics.

contradictions.claimB: Company disclosure attributes much of the increase to customer-receipt timing and lower tax payments.
contradictions.disposition: Resolved as timing sensitivity; use multi-period cash conversion rather than extrapolating the quarter.

unknowns.unknown: Current source-addressed evidence does not establish a material financing/dilution defect.
Supplier concentration by critical component is not quantified in reviewed evidence.
